differences.source_1_mushaf_madinah: أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَرَاهُ ۖ قُلْ فَأْتُوا۟ بِعَشْرِ سُوَرٍۢ مِّثْلِهِۦ مُفْتَرَيَـٰتٍۢ وَٱدْعُوا۟ مَنِ ٱسْتَطَعْتُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَـٰدِقِينَ
differences.source_2_alquran_cloud: أَمْ يَقُولُونَ ٱفْتَرَىٰهُ ۖ قُلْ فَأْتُوا۟ بِعَشْرِ سُوَرٍۢ مِّثْلِهِۦ مُفْتَرَيَٰتٍۢ وَٱدْعُوا۟ مَنِ ٱسْتَطَعْتُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
differences.classification: Orthographic Variation (اختلاف رسم بين طبعة مجمع الملك فهد والطبعة المصرية)
differences.evidence_and_justification: In the King Fahd Glorious Quran Printing Complex (Madinah Mushaf), Hud 13 is written with an explicit Alif Mamdooda (افْتَرَاهُ). In the Egyptian Amiri edition, it is written with an Alef Maqsura bearing a Dagger Alif (ٱفْتَرَىٰهُ). Both represent 100% authentic Uthmani script traditions for Hafs an Asim and are phonetically identical in recitation.

differences.classification: Digital Font Encoding Artifact in External Source (خطأ ترميز رقمي في المصدر الخارجي)
differences.evidence_and_justification: Al-Quran Cloud inserted an erroneous Unicode Dotless Yeh (U+0649) after the Saad (ص) as an unnatural bearer for the dagger alif (صَىٰ). The Madinah Mushaf correctly draws the dagger alif directly over the Saad (صَـٰ) without inserting a phantom letter Yaa. The mapping source is calligraphically accurate.
